✅ Addressed in [`7ae9d7b`](https://github.com/ENTERPILOT/GoModel/commit/7ae9d7b09df27a29822c625658a299edeb9fbe20)

**Failed responses lose partial answers** When Anthropic fails after sending text or tool arguments, `failedEvents` replaces the accumulated output with an empty array and skips closing open items. `responseSnapshotStreamObserver` stores that empty response, and `AssembleResponsesResponse` prefers it over earlier deltas. Users who retrieve the response therefore lose the partial answer they already received. Finish open items as incomplete and include the accumulated output in `response.failed`. **Knowledge Base Used:** [Provider registry and adapters](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=enterpilot&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fenterpilot%2Fgomodel%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fprovider-integration.md)

**Failed requests lose token counts** When Anthropic sends an error after reporting usage in `message_start`, the new failure path drops those captured counts. Previously, `appendTerminalEvents` included them in `response.incomplete`. Earlier translated events carry no usage, so the server's usage observer now records nothing for these requests. Preserve the captured counts in `response.failed` and update `StreamUsageObserver` to read usage from that event too; it currently supports only `response.completed`, `response.done`, and `response.incomplete`. **Knowledge Base Used:** - [Provider registry and adapters](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=enterpilot&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fenterpilot%2Fgomodel%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fprovider-integration.md) - [Streaming and realtime inference](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=enterpilot&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fenterpilot%2Fgomodel%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fstreaming-realtime.md)

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Keep the streamed output in the `response.failed` snapshot.** `failedEvents` sets `output` to an empty array, and `FinishResponse` sends that object unchanged. If the upstream error follows streamed text or a completed tool call, the terminal event drops those items. Consumers that adopt the terminal response object can then store or return the failed turn without its partial output. The response snapshot path for `previous_response_id` is one such consumer. Populate `output` with the items already streamed before the error. Keep `response.failed` as the only terminal event, and do not emit `response.completed` for this turn.
